ctf_name: Module 09 - Adversarial AI and Model Robustness
description: This beginner-friendly CTF challenge builds on Module 08 by exploring advanced adversarial AI (e.g., evasion via feature perturbation) and building robust ML-IDS models. You'll perturb test data to evade detection, then defend with techniques like adversarial training and ensemble models. Educational focus: Learn evasion attacks (changing features to fool models), robustness methods (e.g., training on perturbed data), and metrics like evasion rate. Use the labeled_flows.csv from Module 08; flags from outputs proving defense success (e.g., reduced evasion rate). Submit to validate robustness.

steps.action: Load Poisoned Model from Module 08 and Prepare for Evasion
steps.command: In Python: # Assume model from Mod08; df_test = pd.read_csv('labeled_flows.csv').loc[X_test.index]; # Use test subset
steps.expected_output: df_test ready with original features and labels.
steps.explanation: Evasion is adversarial AI on test data—change features (e.g., reduce packet len) to make attacks look benign without retraining. Education: Unlike poisoning (train-time), evasion is inference-time. Analogy: Disguising a thief at the door vs. bribing the trainer. No flag—setup step.
next_steps: Perform Evasion Attack by Perturbing Features

steps.action: Evasion Attack: Perturb Test Flood Features to Evade Detection
steps.command: In Python: perturbed_test = df_test.copy(); flood_idx = perturbed_test[perturbed_test['label']=='ICMP_FLOOD'].index; perturbed_test.loc[flood_idx, 'ip_len'] *= 0.5; # Halve len to mimic benign; evaded_preds = model.predict(perturbed_test[['proto','ip_len','frame_len']]); evasion_rate = (evaded_preds[flood_idx] == 'Benign').mean(); print(f'Evasion Rate: {evasion_rate:.4f}')
steps.expected_output: Evasion Rate: e.g., 0.7500 (75% floods now classified benign).
steps.explanation: Perturb by modifying features (e.g., smaller packets look less flood-like). Predict on perturbed; high rate=successful evasion. Education: Adversarial AI exploits model boundaries. Analogy: Shrinking a large package to slip past size checks. Flag: Evasion rate, e.g., '0.7500'; submit 'FLAG{Evasion_Rate_0.7500_AttackSucceeds}'.
next_steps: Train Robust Model with Adversarial Training

steps.action: Defend: Train Robust Model Using Adversarial Training
steps.command: In Python: # Augment train with perturbed copies; perturbed_train = X_train.copy(); flood_train_idx = y_train[y_train=='ICMP_FLOOD'].index; perturbed_train.loc[flood_train_idx, 'ip_len'] *= 0.8; # Mild perturb; aug_X = pd.concat([X_train, perturbed_train]); aug_y = pd.concat([y_train, y_train]); robust_model = DecisionTreeClassifier(random_state=42, class_weight='balanced', max_depth=10); robust_model.fit(aug_X, aug_y); robust_preds = robust_model.predict(X_test); robust_acc = accuracy_score(y_test, robust_preds); print(f'Robust Accuracy: {robust_acc:.4f}')
steps.explanation: Adversarial training adds perturbed examples to train, teaching resilience. Limit depth/weight classes. Education: Builds robustness against adversarial AI. Analogy: Training guards with disguised thieves. Higher acc than poisoned. Flag: Robust acc, e.g., '0.9600'; submit 'FLAG{Robust_Acc_0.9600_DefenseStarts}'.
next_steps: Recalculate Evasion Rate on Robust Model

steps.action: Recalculate Evasion Rate on Robust Model
steps.command: In Python: robust_evaded_preds = robust_model.predict(perturbed_test[['proto','ip_len','frame_len']]); robust_evasion_rate = (robust_evaded_preds[flood_idx] == 'Benign').mean(); print(f'Robust Evasion Rate: {robust_evasion_rate:.4f}')
steps.explanation: Reuse perturbed test; low rate shows defense works. Education: Measures robustness to evasion in adversarial AI. Analogy: Disguise fails against trained eyes. Flag: Robust evasion rate, e.g., '0.2000'; submit 'FLAG{Robust_Evasion_0.2000_DefenseStrong}'.

steps.action: Advanced Defense: Use Ensemble of Models for Robustness
steps.command: In Python: from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier; ensemble_model = RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=10, random_state=42, class_weight='balanced'); ensemble_model.fit(aug_X, aug_y); ensemble_preds = ensemble_model.predict(X_test); ensemble_acc = accuracy_score(y_test, ensemble_preds); print(f'Ensemble Accuracy: {ensemble_acc:.4f}')
steps.explanation: RandomForest ensembles multiple trees, averaging for robustness. Education: Ensembles resist adversarial AI by diversity. Analogy: Committee vote harder to fool than one judge. Flag: Ensemble acc, e.g., '0.9800'; submit 'FLAG{Ensemble_Acc_0.9800_RobustWin}'.
next_steps: Final: Generate Confusion Matrix and Extract TP Flag

steps.action: Generate Confusion Matrix for Ensemble and Extract Final Flag
steps.command: In Python: from sklearn.metrics import confusion_matrix; import seaborn as sns; cm = confusion_matrix(y_test, ensemble_preds); sns.heatmap(cm, annot=True, fmt='d'); plt.show(); # TP for ICMP_FLOOD is cm[1,1] assuming index 1=flood; print(cm[1,1])
steps.explanation: Matrix shows classifications; TP=true floods detected. Education: Visualizes robustness in adversarial settings. Analogy: Report card for each threat type. Final proof of defense. Flag: TP value, e.g., '38'; submit 'FLAG{Confusion_TP_38_ModuleComplete}'.
